title: Regex Tester
description: Test JavaScript regular expressions in the browser, see matches, groups, flags, and errors without sending text to the server.
metaDescription: Test JavaScript regular expressions in the browser, inspect matches, captured groups, flags, and errors without sending text to the server.

form.title: Test JavaScript regex
form.description: Type a pattern, paste test text, and inspect matches, groups, and warnings using the browser RegExp engine.

pattern.title: Pattern
pattern.label: Regular expression
pattern.privacy: The pattern and text are processed in the browser. The live link stores only flags and match limit.
pattern.hint: Type without /.../ delimiters. If you paste a JavaScript literal, use the parse-literal button.

examples.text: ana@example.com wrote to support\nbeto@test.dev replied later.

options.title: Flags and limit
options.description: Choose JavaScript flags and how many matches to collect before truncating results.

flags.label: Flags
flags.description: The u and v flags are mutually exclusive. Newer flags depend on the current browser.

descriptions.g: Finds all matches instead of stopping at the first one.
descriptions.m: Makes ^ and $ consider the start and end of each line.
descriptions.v: Enables modern Unicode sets when the browser supports them.
descriptions.y: Matches only from the current last index.
descriptions.d: Exposes match and group indices when the browser supports it.

limit.label: Match limit
limit.description: The limit avoids huge lists and reduces freeze risk.

text.title: Test text
text.description: Paste a sample small enough to test safely.
text.label: Text
text.placeholder: Paste the text that the regex should test.

share.title: Share
share.description: By default, the link stores only flags and limit. Pattern and text enter the # fragment only when you allow it.
share.includeContent: Include pattern and text in the shared link
share.safe: The current link does not include pattern or text.
share.publicWarning: Content links expose the pattern and text to anyone who receives the address.
share.tooLong: The pattern or text is too large for a safe link. The link will include only flags, limit, and the content option.

result.title: Result
result.description: Results follow the browser JavaScript RegExp engine and use UTF-16 indices.
result.processingDescription: The regex is running away from the page so the interface stays responsive.
result.needsTextDescription: Paste test text to run the regex.
result.truncatedDescription: {count} matches shown; results were truncated at the {limit} limit.
result.noMatchDescription: The regex compiled, but found no matches in this text.
result.invalidPatternDescription: Fix the pattern syntax and try again.
result.invalidFlagsDescription: Review duplicated, incompatible, or unsupported flags.
result.patternTooLargeDescription: The pattern exceeds the {limit} character limit.
result.textTooLargeDescription: The text exceeds the automatic {limit} character limit.
result.timeoutDescription: Execution exceeded the time limit and was stopped without blocking the page.

errors.invalidFlags: The selected flags are invalid or incompatible.
errors.unsupportedFlag: One or more flags are not supported by the current browser.
errors.patternTooLarge: The pattern exceeds this tool's limit.
errors.textTooLarge: The text exceeds this tool's limit.

matches.noGroups: This match has no captured groups.
matches.name: Name
matches.indicesAvailable: The d flag exposed indices for this match.

seoDetails.title: Flags, groups, and limits
seoDetails.groupsDescription: Numbered groups appear in parenthesis order. Named groups use JavaScript named-capture syntax and appear in a separate table.
seoDetails.compatibilityDescription: This tester uses browser RegExp. PCRE, Python, Ruby, PHP, and .NET may handle syntax and Unicode differently.
seoDetails.performanceDescription: Some expressions can trigger expensive backtracking. The heuristic warning helps, but does not prove a regex is safe.

privacy.question: Is the text sent to the server?
privacy.answer: No. Compilation and matching run in the browser. Content enters the link only if you enable pattern and text sharing.

engine.question: Which regex engine does this tester use?
engine.answer: It uses the JavaScript RegExp engine available in the current browser.

flags.question: Which JavaScript flags can I use?
flags.answer: The interface offers g, i, m, s, u, v, y, and d. The u and v flags are exclusive, and newer flags depend on browser support.

groups.question: How do I see captured and named groups?
groups.answer: Open the match list. Numbered and named groups appear below each match; with d, indices also appear when supported.

compatibility.question: Why does my regex work on another site but not here?
compatibility.answer: Different engines support different features. This page shows JavaScript behavior, not PCRE or another engine.

performance.question: Can a regex freeze the browser?
performance.answer: Yes. Some backtracking patterns on large inputs can freeze a tab. Use small samples and treat warnings as attention signals.

sharing.question: Can I share a prefilled test?
sharing.answer: Yes, but only by enabling content inclusion. The pattern and text stay in the link fragment and are visible to whoever receives the URL.

seo.about: The regex tester compiles regular expressions with browser JavaScript RegExp and shows matches, captured groups, named groups, selected flags, optional indices, and engine error messages.
seo.howToUse: Type the pattern without delimiters, paste test text, adjust flags, and inspect the match list. Shared links preserve only flags and limit by default; include content only when it can become public.
